title: How did public administration research change?
dek: Follow five journals from the research map to a comparison of two five-year cohorts, then see which shifts hold when the inputs change.

steps.heading: Read the map one paper at a time
steps.text: Each dot represents a research article or review from five journals published between 1980 and 2025. Nearby dots tend to share vocabulary. Colours mark ten groups of papers. The analysis used 8,874 available abstracts plus the titles of all 10,606 papers.

steps.heading: Start where all five journals overlap
steps.text: The five current journal titles share a publication window starting in 2001. The first five years contain 939 papers and 870 usable abstracts. The map shows that cohort at its original positions.

steps.heading: Move the same map forward twenty years
steps.text: The recent five-year cohort contains 2,016 papers and 1,978 usable abstracts. With more than twice as many papers, topic shares tell us how the mix changed even as publication volume grew.

steps.heading: The early leader lost share
steps.text: Comparative Governance and Administrative Reform was the largest group in 2001–2005, at 26.4% of the cohort. Its share fell to 7.1% in 2021–2025. This direction appears within each of the five journals.

steps.heading: Collaboration gained ground in all five journals
steps.text: Collaborative Governance and Citizen Participation rose from 8.9% to 18.9% of papers. The increase appears within every journal, alongside the shift in the pooled comparison.

steps.heading: Workforce research rose, too
steps.text: Public Workforces, Leadership and Representation went from 8.3% to 16.0%. The two rising themes together account for 704 of the 2,016 recent papers, just under 35%.

steps.heading: The direction persists across inputs
steps.text: The same directions appear when titles alone are assigned to the fitted topic groups and when the original assignments are restricted to papers with usable abstracts. The estimated size of each shift varies.

steps.heading: The journals changed what they emphasised
steps.text: Between 2001–2005 and 2021–2025, these five journals devoted a larger share of papers to collaboration, participation and public workforces, and a smaller share to comparative governance and administrative reform. This describes changes in the mix of published research under the atlas’s topic model.

end.title: Follow a topic to the papers behind it
